title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web

        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS

        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port

        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user

| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073", "CVE-2024-3400", "CVE-2023-4966", "CVE-2020-5135")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073", "CVE-2024-3400", "CVE-2023-4966", "CVE-2020-5135")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073", "CVE-2024-3400", "CVE-2023-4966", "CVE-2020-5135")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073", "CVE-2024-3400", "CVE-2023-4966", "CVE-2020-5135")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["025fc0976c548fb5a880c83ea3eb21a5f23c5d53c4e51e862bb893c11adf712a", "1334f0189a8e6dbc48456fa4b482c5726ab7609f7fa652fcc4c1a96f2334436f", "1af419b36a5edefef387409e2b3248c9223f7dc49a4f7b15ea095d371c3a70b2", "22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "24ac3588fb8cfbff63b7fdfcbc7dec1f3c60e54e6f949dd69d68e89e0c89d966", "2ed9494e9b7b68415b4eb151c922c82c0191294d0aa443dd2cb5133e6bfe3d5d", "3ab9575225e00a83a4ac2b534da5a710bdcf6eb72884944c437b5fbe5c5c9235", "3c2182cb0bc7528829ef03f1b1745a92bcc47d917eb8870862488f21fdf1a6d6", "1eece1e1ba4b96e6c784729f0608ad2939cfb67bc4236dfababbe1d09268960c", "5dc607c8990841139768884b1b43e1403496d5a458788a1937be139594f01dca", "788ba200f776a188c248d6c2029f00b5d34be45d4444f7cb89ffe838c39b8b19"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Google DoubleClick Abused in New Malspam Campaign to Deliver DesckVB RAT

The Hacker News
2026-06-03 16 use cases 8 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have flagged a new malspam campaign that makes use of Google's DoubleClick domain as a way to evade detection and ultimately deliver a remote access trojan (RAT) named DesckVB RAT. "Before the victim ever reaches attacker-controlled infrastructure, the lure routes through DoubleClick, a legitimate Google-owned domain that many security tools are less likely to treat as

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] HTML attachment with meta-refresh redirect via Google DoubleClick to malspam landing · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] ZIP-borne JavaScript loader spawning PowerShell from user Downloads · [LLM] DesckVB Defender exclusion configuration via Add-MpPreference / WMIC · [LLM] DesckVB persistence via Run/RunOnce + Startup folder loader drop · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] PowerShell fetching DesckVB .NET loader from pastee.dev · [LLM] DesckVB C2 raw TCP beacon to known infrastructure (IPs + DDNS + hostgator domain) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] HTML attachment with meta-refresh redirect via Google DoubleClick to malspam landing Delivery Medium
Hunts the DesckVB delivery vector: phishing email with an .html attachment that meta-refreshes the browser through a doubleclick.net click-tracking URL into an attacker-controlled redirector. Pivots EmailAttachmentInfo (.html) joined with UrlClickEvents to doubleclick.net within a small window. Rationale: Article explicitly states the HTML attachment 'triggers a meta-refresh browser redirect to a Google DoubleClick Campaign Manager click-tracking URL'. The HTML + doubleclick.net pivot within a tight time window is the distinguishing signal — generic doubleclick traffic from ad-loaded browsing isn't preceded by an email-attached HTML open. Cross-checked against: • https://www.huntress.com/blog/desckvb-rat-malspam
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.001 T1102
Data sourcesEmail.Email_Attachments Web.Web
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let HtmlAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName endswith ".html" or FileName endswith ".htm"
    | project EmailTime = Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress, FileName, SHA256;
let DoubleClickClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where Url has_any ("doubleclick.net", "ad.doubleclick.net", "googleadservices.com")
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed", "ClickedThrough");
HtmlAttachments
| join kind=inner DoubleClickClicks on $left.RecipientEmailAddress == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 30m)
| project EmailTime, ClickTime = Timestamp, RecipientEmailAddress, FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256, Url, NetworkMessageId
| order by EmailTime desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let PhishedRecipients = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where Operation has_any ("FileMalwareDetected", "AttachmentDetected")
    | distinct UserId;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where Url has_any ("doubleclick.net/click", "ad.doubleclick.net", "googleadservices.com/pagead")
| where SrcUsername in (PhishedRecipients) or HttpRequestHeaderReferer has_any (".html", ".htm")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, HttpRequestHeaderReferer, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DstHostname
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(windows.defender OR azure.activeDirectory) (@evt.name:EmailAttachmentInfo OR @evt.name:UrlClickEvents) (@FileName:(*.html OR *.htm) OR @Url:(*doubleclick.net* OR *ad.doubleclick.net*))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/doubleclick\.net|googleadservices\.com/i
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/outlook\.exe|chrome\.exe|msedge\.exe/i CommandLine=/\.html?/i}, field=aid)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName], function=count())
WEB

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Email where Email.file_name="*.html" OR Email.file_name="*.htm" by Email.src_user Email.recipient Email.message_id Email.file_name Email.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Email)` | join type=inner message_id [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web where Web.url="*doubleclick.net*" OR Web.url="*ad.doubleclick.net*" by Web.src Web.user Web.url Web.message_id | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`] | where lastTime - firstTime < 600
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Email where Email.file_name="*.html" OR Email.file_name="*.htm" by Email.src_user Email.recipient Email.message_id Email.file_name Email.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Email)` | join type=inner message_id [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where Web.url="*doubleclick.net*" OR Web.url="*ad.doubleclick.net*" by Web.src Web.user Web.url Web.message_id | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`] | where lastTime - firstTime < 600
[LLM] ZIP-borne JavaScript loader spawning PowerShell from user Downloads Installation High
Hunts the second-stage DesckVB execution: ZIP archive downloaded from the malspam landing page contains a .js file that wscript.exe/cscript.exe runs, which then extracts and launches PowerShell to fetch the .NET loader. Detects the Downloads-folder JS → PowerShell parent-child chain. Rationale: Article: 'a JavaScript loader, whose main responsibility is to retrieve and execute a .NET RAT... The script extracts and runs a PowerShell script'. The Downloads/Temp parent-path constraint plus the wscript→powershell chain is the load-bearing combination from the article's ZIP-attached-from-landing-page narrative. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/007/
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1059.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wscript.exe", "cscript.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "cmd.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (".js", ".jse", ".vbs", ".wsf")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("explorer.exe", "7zG.exe", "WinRAR.exe", "7zFM.exe", "chrome.exe", "msedge.exe", "firefox.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          GrandparentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe", "cscript.exe")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "cmd.exe")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (".js", ".jse", ".vbs", ".wsf")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: ZIP-borne JS Loader Spawning PowerShell from Downloads (DesckVB)
id: 7d4e2c91-3a8f-4b62-9d1e-5f8a2c7b9d10
description: Detects wscript.exe or cscript.exe in the user Downloads/Temp path spawning PowerShell — the DesckVB RAT delivery chain seen in the Huntress June 2026 DoubleClick malspam campaign.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/google-doubleclick-abused-in-new.html
author: SOC Detection Team
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1204.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - '.js'
      - '.jse'
      - '.vbs'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
  selection_path:
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - '\Downloads\'
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\Roaming\'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_path
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate enterprise scripts launched manually by power users
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\wscript.exe OR *\WScript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\CScript.exe) @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe) @ParentCommandLine:(*.js* OR *.vbs*) @ParentCommandLine:(*\Downloads\* OR *\Temp\* OR *\AppData\*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd)\.exe$/i
| regex("\\\\(Downloads|Temp|AppData\\\\(Local|Roaming))\\\\", field=ParentCommandLine)
| regex("\\.(js|jse|vbs|wsf)", field=ParentCommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, ParentCommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") AND Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" AND (Processes.parent_process LIKE "%\\Downloads\\%" OR Processes.parent_process LIKE "%\\Temp\\%" OR Processes.parent_process LIKE "%.js%") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") AND Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" AND (Processes.parent_process LIKE "%\\Downloads\\%" OR Processes.parent_process LIKE "%\\Temp\\%" OR Processes.parent_process LIKE "%.js%") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
[LLM] PowerShell fetching DesckVB .NET loader from pastee.dev Command & Control High
Hunts the stager retrieval step: PowerShell making outbound HTTPS to pastee.dev (the article-named payload-hosting service) to download the .NET loader. The pastee.dev domain is specific to this campaign and not a common enterprise destination. Rationale: pastee.dev is explicitly listed as IOC infrastructure. PowerShell → pastee.dev outbound is rarely a legitimate enterprise pattern (paste-share sites aren't typical PowerShell module sources). Bound to specific named binary + named domain = high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/google-doubleclick-abused-in-new.html
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has "pastee.dev" or RemoteUrl endswith "pastee.dev"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DstHostname has "pastee.dev" or Url has "pastee.dev"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: PowerShell Outbound to pastee.dev (DesckVB Loader Fetch)
id: 1a7f8e92-c4b3-4d27-9e1a-6c5b8a3d7e22
description: Detects powershell.exe initiating an outbound connection to pastee.dev — the payload-hosting domain used to deliver the DesckVB .NET loader.

| DomainName=/pastee\.dev$/i OR RemoteAddressIP4=/^(23\.186\.113\.60|45\.156\.87\.226)$/

[LLM] DesckVB Defender exclusion configuration via Add-MpPreference / WMIC Installation High
Hunts DesckVB's tamper step where the loader 'configures Microsoft Defender exclusions' before dropping the RAT. Detects Add-MpPreference / Set-MpPreference with ExclusionPath/ExclusionProcess from non-admin process contexts spawned by the malspam chain. Rationale: Article: 'neutralizes the machine's security controls' and 'configures Microsoft Defender exclusions'. The Add-MpPreference + Exclusion* combination is the canonical realisation. Filtering on non-GPO parents removes the legitimate admin path and keeps the loader-driven path. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/001/
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "cmd.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Add-MpPreference", "Set-MpPreference")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("ExclusionPath", "ExclusionProcess", "ExclusionExtension", "DisableRealtimeMonitoring", "DisableIOAVProtection", "DisableBehaviorMonitoring")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("gpscript.exe", "SenseIR.exe", "MsSense.exe", "MpCmdRun.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          InitiatingImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ProcessCommandLine,
          ProcessIntegrityLevel
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "cmd.exe")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("Add-MpPreference", "Set-MpPreference")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("ExclusionPath", "ExclusionProcess", "ExclusionExtension", "DisableRealtimeMonitoring", "DisableBehaviorMonitoring")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName !has_any ("gpscript.exe", "MsSense.exe", "MpCmdRun.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Defender Exclusion Added by Non-Admin Tooling (DesckVB Tamper)
id: 9b3c4d8e-2f5a-4e71-b8c2-7d4e9f1a6b35
description: Detects Add-MpPreference / Set-MpPreference with ExclusionPath/ExclusionProcess/DisableRealtimeMonitoring, scoped to non-GPO parents — matches DesckVB loader behaviour described in Huntress June 2026 report.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/google-doubleclick-abused-in-new.html
author: SOC Detection Team
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1562.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_exec:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Add-MpPreference'
      - 'Set-MpPreference'
  selection_args:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'ExclusionPath'
      - 'ExclusionProcess'
      - 'ExclusionExtension'
      - 'DisableRealtimeMonitoring'
      - 'DisableBehaviorMonitoring'
  filter_legit:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\gpscript.exe'
      - '\MsSense.exe'
      - '\MpCmdRun.exe'
  condition: selection_exec and selection_cmd and selection_args and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
  - Sysadmins manually adding exclusions during AV exception requests
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\cmd.exe) (@CommandLine:*Add-MpPreference* OR @CommandLine:*Set-MpPreference*) (@CommandLine:*ExclusionPath* OR @CommandLine:*ExclusionProcess* OR @CommandLine:*DisableRealtimeMonitoring*) -@ParentImage:(*\gpscript.exe OR *\MsSense.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd)\.exe$/i
| regex("(Add|Set)-MpPreference", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(ExclusionPath|ExclusionProcess|ExclusionExtension|DisableRealtimeMonitoring|DisableBehaviorMonitoring)", field=CommandLine)
| NOT ParentBaseFileName=/^(gpscript|MsSense|MpCmdRun)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe") AND (Processes.process LIKE "%Add-MpPreference%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%Set-MpPreference%") AND (Processes.process LIKE "%ExclusionPath%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%ExclusionProcess%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%ExclusionExtension%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%DisableRealtimeMonitoring%") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe") AND (Processes.process LIKE "%Add-MpPreference%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%Set-MpPreference%") AND (Processes.process LIKE "%ExclusionPath%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%ExclusionProcess%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%ExclusionExtension%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%DisableRealtimeMonitoring%") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
[LLM] DesckVB persistence via Run/RunOnce + Startup folder loader drop Installation Medium
Hunts the DesckVB persistence step: registry Run/RunOnce write OR a binary placed in the user Startup folder by a process descended from the PowerShell loader chain. The article calls out both vectors as part of the same install step. Rationale: Article: 'persistence is established on the host by setting up Run and RunOnce Registry entries, along with placing a loader responsible for launching the RAT in the user's Startup folder'. The dual-path detection covers both vectors as one logical unit. Constrains to script-host parents to avoid noisy installer hits. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/
ATT&CKT1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Filesystem
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let RunKeys = DeviceRegistryEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet", "RegistryKeyCreated")
    | where RegistryKey has_any (@"\CurrentVersion\Run", @"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce")
    | where RegistryValueData has_any (@"\AppData\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Temp\", @"\Public\")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "cmd.exe", "regsvr32.exe", "rundll32.exe")
    | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, 
              Vector = "RunKey", 
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              Image = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              ImageCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              KeyPath = RegistryKey,
              ValueName = RegistryValueName,
              ValueData = RegistryValueData;
let StartupDrops = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed")
    | where FolderPath has @"\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "cmd.exe")
    | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              Vector = "StartupFolder",
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              Image = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              ImageCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              KeyPath = FolderPath,
              ValueName = FileName,
              ValueData = SHA256;
RunKeys
| union StartupDrops
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let RunKeys = ImRegistryEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where RegistryKey has_any (@"\CurrentVersion\Run", @"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce")
    | where RegistryValueData has_any (@"\AppData\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Temp\", @"\Public\")
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "cmd.exe")
    | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Vector = "RunKey",
              ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
              RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData;
let StartupDrops = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where TargetFilePath has @"\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\"
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "cmd.exe")
    | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Vector = "StartupFolder",
              ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
              RegistryKey = TargetFilePath, RegistryValue = TargetFileName, RegistryValueData = TargetFileSHA256;
RunKeys
| union StartupDrops
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 @TargetObject:(*\CurrentVersion\Run\* OR *\CurrentVersion\RunOnce\*) @Details:(*\AppData\* OR *\ProgramData\* OR *\Temp\*) @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe)) OR (source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\Start*Menu\Programs\Startup\* OR *\Start*Menu\Programs\StartUp\*) @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe))
(#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate RegObjectName=/\\CurrentVersion\\Run(Once)?$/i RegStringValue=/\\(AppData|ProgramData|Temp|Public)\\/i ContextImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|cmd)\.exe$/i)
OR (#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup\\/i ContextImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|cmd)\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RegObjectName, RegStringValue, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
(| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where (Registry.registry_path LIKE "%\\CurrentVersion\\Run%" OR Registry.registry_path LIKE "%\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce%") AND (Registry.registry_value_data LIKE "%\\AppData\\%" OR Registry.registry_value_data LIKE "%\\ProgramData\\%" OR Registry.registry_value_data LIKE "%\\Temp\\%") AND Registry.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe") by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.process_name Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`) | append [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path LIKE "%\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup\\%" AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`]
(| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where (Registry.registry_path LIKE "%\\CurrentVersion\\Run%" OR Registry.registry_path LIKE "%\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce%") AND (Registry.registry_value_data LIKE "%\\AppData\\%" OR Registry.registry_value_data LIKE "%\\ProgramData\\%" OR Registry.registry_value_data LIKE "%\\Temp\\%") AND Registry.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe") by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.process_name Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`) | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path LIKE "%\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup\\%" AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`]
[LLM] DesckVB C2 raw TCP beacon to known infrastructure (IPs + DDNS + hostgator domain) Command & Control High
Hunts the DesckVB RAT's command-and-control channel: raw TCP outbound to article-published infrastructure — 23.186.113.60, 45.156.87.226, manikandan83.mysynology.net (DDNS), or the long meusitehostgator.com.br subdomain. Triggers on any internal host reaching any of these endpoints from any process. Rationale: Direct IOC hit list from the article's pre-extracted IOCs. The mysynology.net DDNS + the unusually long 1552093.meusitehostgator.com.br subdomain are both campaign-specific. Even one DNS query to these names from an internal host is alert-worthy. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/google-doubleclick-abused-in-new.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1095
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
let DesckVBIPs = dynamic(["23.186.113.60", "45.156.87.226"]);
let DesckVBDomains = dynamic(["manikandan83.mysynology.net", "andrefelipedonascime1768785037020.1552093.meusitehostgator.com.br", "pastee.dev"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (DesckVBIPs)
    or RemoteUrl has_any (DesckVBDomains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let DesckVBIPs = dynamic(["23.186.113.60", "45.156.87.226"]);
let DesckVBDomains = dynamic(["manikandan83.mysynology.net", "andrefelipedonascime1768785037020.1552093.meusitehostgator.com.br", "pastee.dev"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in (DesckVBIPs)
    or DstHostname in~ (DesckVBDomains)
    or Url has_any (DesckVBDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername,
          DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol,
          NetworkBytes, NetworkDuration, Url
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: DesckVB RAT C2 Beacon to Known Infrastructure
id: 4f8a2b71-9c3d-4e85-a1b6-7e9f3c4d8b21
description: Detects outbound network traffic to article-published DesckVB RAT C2 infrastructure (Huntress June 2026 DoubleClick malspam campaign).
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/google-doubleclick-abused-in-new.html
author: SOC Detection Team
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1095
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_ip:
    DestinationIp:
      - '23.186.113.60'
      - '45.156.87.226'
  selection_domain:
    DestinationHostname:
      - 'manikandan83.mysynology.net'

(#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4=/^(23\.186\.113\.60|45\.156\.87\.226)$/) OR (#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/^(manikandan83\.mysynology\.net|andrefelipedonascime1768785037020\.1552093\.meusitehostgator\.com\.br|pastee\.dev)$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, DomainName, RemotePort], function=count())
| sort([aid, ComputerName], order=asc)
# log group: /aws/vpc/flowlogs
fields @timestamp, srcAddr, dstAddr, srcPort, dstPort, protocol, action, bytes
| filter dstAddr in ["23.186.113.60", "45.156.87.226"] or srcAddr in ["23.186.113.60", "45.156.87.226"]
| filter action = "ACCEPT"
| stats sum(bytes) as totalBytes, count(*) as flows by srcAddr, dstAddr, dstPort, protocol

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic where (Network_Traffic.dest IN ("23.186.113.60","45.156.87.226") OR Network_Traffic.dest_host IN ("manikandan83.mysynology.net","andrefelipedonascime1768785037020.1552093.meusitehostgator.com.br","pastee.dev") OR Network_Traffic.url="*manikandan83.mysynology.net*" OR Network_Traffic.url="*1552093.meusitehostgator.com.br*") by Network_Traffic.src Network_Traffic.user Network_Traffic.dest Network_Traffic.dest_host Network_Traffic.dest_port Network_Traffic.transport Network_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(Network_Traffic)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url

     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High

Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents

| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental
description: |

    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    category: process_creation

            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'

        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'

            - 'invoke-expression'

| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")

SecurityEvent

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:

            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:

Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] CVE-2022-0492 — Write to cgroup release_agent file inside /sys/fs/cgroup hierarchy

[LLM] CVE-2022-0492 cgroup release_agent container escape — unshare + rdma mount + release_agent chain Exploitation High
Hunts the published exploit signature for CVE-2022-0492: a process inside a container invokes 'unshare' to create user/cgroup namespaces and then mounts the RDMA cgroup controller, with a command line referencing the cgroup 'release_agent' file. This is the exact behavioural chain documented by Aqua Security, Palo Alto Unit 42 and Sysdig for the CISA-KEV-listed Linux kernel container escape. Rationale: Anchored on the published Falco/Sysdig rule for CVE-2022-0492 (unshare + mount + rdma + release_agent) and the Aqua / Unit 42 exploit walkthrough that the article explicitly cites. Cross-checked Unit 42 (https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cve-2022-0492-cgroups/), Aqua Security blog, and Sysdig (https://www.sysdig.com/blog/detecting-mitigating-cve-2022-0492-sysdig). The 'release_agent' string + 'rdma' cgroup controller combo is article-specific and not matched by generic LOLBin / privilege-escalation rules. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cve-2022-0492-cgroups/ • https://www.aquasec.com/blog/new-linux-kernel-vulnerability-escaping-containers-by-abusing-cgroups/ • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/detecting-mitigating-cve-2022-0492-sysdig • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2022-0492 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/
ATT&CKT1611 T1068 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName == "unshare" or InitiatingProcessFileName == "unshare" or ProcessCommandLine has "unshare"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "release_agent"
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "mount" and ProcessCommandLine has "rdma" and ProcessCommandLine has "cgroup")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "unshare" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)-[UrmC]+|--user|--mount|--cgroup")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/unshare" or ActingProcessName =~ "unshare" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "unshare"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "release_agent"
   or (ActingProcessCommandLine has "mount" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "rdma" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "cgroup")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: CVE-2022-0492 cgroup release_agent Container Escape via unshare
id: 7b3e8c1d-6a4f-4e21-9b8d-1f2a5c3d9e10
description: Detects the published CVE-2022-0492 exploit chain where a process uses unshare to create user/cgroup namespaces and mounts the rdma cgroup controller with a command line referencing the cgroup release_agent file. Pattern from Aqua Security, Unit 42 and Sysdig writeups.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cve-2022-0492-cgroups/
  - https://www.aquasec.com/blog/new-linux-kernel-vulnerability-escaping-containers-by-abusing-cgroups/
  - https://www.sysdig.com/blog/detecting-mitigating-cve-2022-0492-sysdig
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisa-warns-of-active-attacks-exploiting-android-linux-bugs/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1611
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.privilege_escalation
  - cve.2022.0492
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_unshare:
    Image|endswith: '/unshare'
  selection_chain:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'release_agent'
  selection_mount:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'mount'
      - 'rdma'
      - 'cgroup'
  condition: selection_unshare and (selection_chain or selection_mount)
falsepositives:
  - Container security research / pentesting
  - Kubernetes upgrade tooling that legitimately remounts cgroupfs
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.name:unshare OR @process.command_line:*unshare*) (@process.command_line:*release_agent* OR (@process.command_line:*rdma* AND @process.command_line:*cgroup*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ImageFileName=/\/unshare$/i OR CommandLine=/unshare/i)
| (CommandLine=/release_agent/i OR (CommandLine=/rdma/i AND CommandLine=/cgroup/i))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="unshare" OR Processes.process="*unshare*") AND (Processes.process="*release_agent*" OR (Processes.process="*mount*" AND Processes.process="*rdma*" AND Processes.process="*cgroup*")) by Processes.dest Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="unshare" OR Processes.process="*unshare*") AND (Processes.process="*release_agent*" OR (Processes.process="*mount*" AND Processes.process="*rdma*" AND Processes.process="*cgroup*")) by Processes.dest Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] CVE-2022-0492 — Write to cgroup release_agent file inside /sys/fs/cgroup hierarchy Installation High
Detects creation or modification of a 'release_agent' file inside the cgroup filesystem — the terminal step of the CVE-2022-0492 container-escape chain where the attacker plants a command (executed as root on the host) into release_agent and triggers notify_on_release. Article cross-referenced Aqua Security + Unit 42 research on this exact primitive. Rationale: release_agent is a cgroups v1-specific primitive — there is almost no benign reason for non-runtime code to write to it. Anchored on the article's named function (cgroup_release_agent_write) plus the Unit 42 / Aqua exploit chain (https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cve-2022-0492-cgroups/). Detects the terminal step of the exploit even if the attacker writes from a shell rather than unshare directly (covering UC1's blind spots). Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cve-2022-0492-cgroups/ • https://www.aquasec.com/blog/new-linux-kernel-vulnerability-escaping-containers-by-abusing-cgroups/ • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/detecting-mitigating-cve-2022-0492-sysdig • https://book.hacktricks.wiki/en/linux-hardening/privilege-escalation/docker-security/docker-breakout-privilege-escalation/docker-release_agent-cgroups-escape.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/
ATT&CKT1611 T1574 T1547
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName == "release_agent"
| where FolderPath has "/sys/fs/cgroup/" or FolderPath has "/cgroup/"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("systemd", "kubelet", "containerd", "containerd-shim", "runc", "crun", "dockerd")
             and InitiatingProcessAccountName == "root")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FileName, FolderPath, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFileName == "release_agent"
| where TargetFilePath has "/sys/fs/cgroup/" or TargetFilePath has "/cgroup/"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileWritten")
| where not (ActingProcessName has_any ("systemd", "kubelet", "containerd", "runc", "crun", "dockerd")
             and ActorUsername == "root")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: CVE-2022-0492 cgroup release_agent File Write
id: 9f4a2c7e-3d8b-4c5a-a6f1-2e8d9b3c4f50
description: Detects creation or modification of a release_agent file inside the /sys/fs/cgroup hierarchy. This is the persistence/trigger primitive of the CVE-2022-0492 container escape — the file is invoked by the kernel as root on the host when notify_on_release fires.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cve-2022-0492-cgroups/
  - https://www.aquasec.com/blog/new-linux-kernel-vulnerability-escaping-containers-by-abusing-cgroups/
  - https://terenceli.github.io/%E6%8A%80%E6%9C%AF/2022/03/06/cve-2022-0492
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisa-warns-of-active-attacks-exploiting-android-linux-bugs/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1611
  - attack.t1574
  - attack.privilege_escalation
  - cve.2022.0492
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '/release_agent'
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/sys/fs/cgroup/'
      - '/cgroup/'
  filter_runtime:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/systemd'
      - '/kubelet'
      - '/containerd'
      - '/containerd-shim'
      - '/runc'
      - '/crun'
      - '/dockerd'
  condition: selection and not filter_runtime
falsepositives:
  - Container runtime startup (filtered above)
  - Manual sysadmin tuning of legacy cgroup v1 notify_on_release behaviour
level: high
source:linux.auditd (@file.path:*\/sys\/fs\/cgroup\/*\/release_agent OR @file.path:*\/cgroup\/*\/release_agent) (@auditd.type:PATH OR @evt.name:open OR @evt.name:openat OR @evt.name:write) -@process.name:(systemd OR kubelet OR containerd OR containerd-shim OR runc OR crun OR dockerd)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| regex("\\/release_agent$", field=TargetFileName)
| regex("\\/(sys\\/fs\\/)?cgroup\\/", field=TargetFileName)
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/\/(systemd|kubelet|containerd|containerd-shim|runc|crun|dockerd)$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as process values(Filesystem.user) as user values(Filesystem.action) as action from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="release_agent" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/release_agent") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*/sys/fs/cgroup/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/cgroup/*") AND Filesystem.action IN ("create","modify","write","created","modified") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-48595", "CVE-2022-0492")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has

// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-48595", "CVE-2022-0492")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beyond the Zero-Day: See Your Network Like an Attacker | Webinar with HD Moore

The Hacker News
2026-06-03 9 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

A development flag left switched on in production builds of several Microsoft 365 Android apps disabled the check that limits account-token sharing to trusted Microsoft apps. Any other app on the same phone could ask for the signed-in user's token and get it, then read email, open files, browse the calendar, and send messages as that user. No password, no login screen, no permission prompt.

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Unpatched Microsoft 365 Android apps below FlagLeft fix build 16.0.19822.20190
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] FOCI refresh-token sign-in from non-compliant Android device (FlagLeft post-theft replay) · [LLM] FOCI cross-app token chaining: one Android device authenticates to 3+ affected Office mobile apps · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Unpatched Microsoft 365 Android apps below FlagLeft fix build 16.0.19822.20190 Installation High
Inventory hunt for Android devices running vulnerable Word/PowerPoint/Excel/Copilot/OneNote/Loop builds older than the FlagLeft patch (16.0.19822.20190). Surfaces the population that needs MDM-forced update and refresh-token revocation, regardless of whether exploitation occurred. Rationale: Pivots on the exact patched build number (16.0.19822.20190) and the four CVE IDs Microsoft assigned on May 12. TVM is the primary source for mobile app version inventory; Intune fallback advised for tenants without Defender for Endpoint on Android.
ATT&CKT1528 T1474.002
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
// FlagLeft — Android devices on a Microsoft 365 build older than 16.0.19822.20190
DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
| where OSPlatform =~ "Android"
| where SoftwareVendor has "Microsoft"
| where SoftwareName has_any ("Word","PowerPoint","Excel","Microsoft 365 Copilot","Copilot","OneNote","Loop")
| extend Parts = split(SoftwareVersion, ".")
| extend Major = toint(Parts[0]), Minor = toint(Parts[1]), Build = toint(Parts[2]), Revision = toint(Parts[3])
| where Major == 16 and Minor == 0 and (Build < 19822 or (Build == 19822 and Revision < 20190))
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | where OSPlatform =~ "Android" | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, LoggedOnUsers, IsAzureADJoined, JoinType) by DeviceId) on DeviceId

[LLM] FOCI refresh-token sign-in from non-compliant Android device (FlagLeft post-theft replay) Actions on Objectives Medium
Catches the replay pattern an attacker would produce after stealing FOCI tokens via FlagLeft: a refresh-token (non-interactive) sign-in to one of the affected Office mobile apps from an Android device that is NOT Intune-managed/compliant/AAD-joined. Legitimate users on managed devices have DeviceTrustType set; a stolen token replayed from the attacker's device will not. Rationale: FlagLeft's stolen artefact is a FOCI Family Refresh Token. The attacker's replay shows as a non-interactive sign-in (ErrorCode 0, IsInteractive=false) to one of the six specifically affected Office mobile apps, on Android, from a device that — being the attacker's device — has no AAD device trust. Legitimate FOCI refresh on the victim's actual device carries Compliant/Managed/AzureAd trust type once enrolled.
ATT&CKT1528 T1550.001 T1606.002
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
// FlagLeft replay — FOCI refresh from unmanaged Android into an affected M365 mobile app
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where OSPlatform =~ "Android"
| where Application in~ ("Microsoft Word","Microsoft PowerPoint","Microsoft Excel","Microsoft 365 Copilot","Microsoft OneNote","Microsoft Loop","Microsoft Office")
| where ErrorCode == 0                              // successful auth
| where IsInteractive == false                       // refresh-token (FOCI FRT) flow, not a password sign-in
| where (DeviceTrustType !in~ ("Compliant","Managed","AzureAd","Workplace")) or isempty(DeviceTrustType)
| where AccountUpn !endswith "#EXT#" and not(AccountUpn endswith "$")
| extend DayCountForUser = toscalar(AADSignInEventsBeta | where Timestamp between (ago(30d) .. ago(7d)) | where AccountUpn == AccountUpn | summarize dcount(bin(Timestamp,1d)))
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, Application, ApplicationId, IPAddress, Country, City, UserAgent, OSPlatform, DeviceTrustType, IsCompliantUser, AadDeviceId, ClientAppUsed, RiskLevelDuringSignIn, RiskState, TokenIssuerType
| order by Timestamp desc
// FlagLeft replay — FOCI refresh from unmanaged Android into an affected M365 mobile app
let AffectedApps = dynamic(["Microsoft Word","Microsoft PowerPoint","Microsoft Excel","Microsoft 365 Copilot","Microsoft OneNote","Microsoft Loop","Microsoft Office"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (SigninLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)),
  (AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d))
| where AppDisplayName in~ (AffectedApps)
| extend DeviceOS = tostring(DeviceDetail.operatingSystem),
         DeviceIsCompliant = tobool(DeviceDetail.isCompliant),
         DeviceIsManaged = tobool(DeviceDetail.isManaged),
         DeviceTrustTypeParsed = tostring(DeviceDetail.trustType),
         DeviceIdParsed = tostring(DeviceDetail.deviceId)
| where DeviceOS has "Android"
| where ResultType == 0                              // successful
| where IsInteractive == false                        // FRT replay
| where (DeviceIsCompliant != true) and (DeviceIsManaged != true)
| where isempty(DeviceTrustTypeParsed) or DeviceTrustTypeParsed !in~ ("Compliant","Managed","AzureAd","Workplace")
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, AppId, IPAddress, Location, UserAgent, DeviceOS, DeviceTrustTypeParsed, DeviceIdParsed, ClientAppUsed, RiskLevelDuringSignIn, RiskState, ConditionalAccessStatus, AuthenticationRequirement
| order by TimeGenerated desc
