level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon OR cloudtrail) (@network.destination.ip:169.254.169.254 OR @DestinationIp:169.254.169.254 OR @network.destination.host:(metadata.google.internal OR metadata.azure.com) OR @DestinationHostname:(metadata.google.internal OR *.vault.azure.net)) (@process.name:(node OR bun) OR @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\bun.exe OR */node OR */bun))
(#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 OR #event_simpleName=DnsRequest)
| (RemoteAddressIP4="169.254.169.254" OR DomainName=/metadata\.(google\.internal|azure\.com)/i OR DomainName=/.*\.vault\.azure\.net$/i)
| ContextImageFileName=/\/(node|bun)(\.exe)?$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId, DomainName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())
# log group: /aws/vpc/flowlogs
fields @timestamp, srcAddr, dstAddr, dstPort, action, bytes
| filter dstAddr = "169.254.169.254"
      and action = "ACCEPT"
| stats count(*) as imdsCalls, sum(bytes) as totalBytes by srcAddr, bin(5m)
| sort @timestamp desc
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest="169.254.169.254" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="metadata.google.internal") AND (All_Traffic.process_name="node" OR All_Traffic.process_name="node.exe" OR All_Traffic.process_name="bun" OR All_Traffic.process_name="bun.exe") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.process | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest="169.254.169.254" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="metadata.google.internal") AND (All_Traffic.process_name="node" OR All_Traffic.process_name="node.exe" OR All_Traffic.process_name="bun" OR All_Traffic.process_name="bun.exe") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.process | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] Passwordless sudo rule dropped into /etc/sudoers.d (Miasma privilege escalation) Exploitation High
Detects creation of files under /etc/sudoers.d containing 'NOPASSWD:ALL' (specifically the 'runner ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' string the Miasma payload writes), and the bind-mount-to-/mnt technique used to deposit the sudoers fragment. Sigma covers the process-create path; KQL covers both file-write and sudoers-validation chains. Rationale: Anchored on the article's exact verbatim code block: "echo 'runner ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' > ... && chmod 0440 /mnt/runner" and "sudo -n true". The 'NOPASSWD:ALL' string combined with a /etc/sudoers.d or /mnt/ write target is the article-specific signature; this rule should not fire on legitimate config-mgmt because we filter on node/bun/shell parents.
ATT&CKT1548.003 T1098
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "NOPASSWD:ALL"
       and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/etc/sudoers.d","/mnt/","sudoers")
    | extend Source = "ProcessCreate"),
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FolderPath startswith "/etc/sudoers.d/"
       or (FolderPath startswith "/mnt/" and FileName has_any ("runner","sudoers"))
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun","sh","bash","dash","tee","cp","mv","dd")
    | extend Source = "FileWrite", ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName_proc = InitiatingProcessFileName)
| project Timestamp, Source, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
union
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "NOPASSWD:ALL"
       and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/etc/sudoers.d","/mnt/","sudoers")
    | extend Source = "ProcessCreate"),
  (ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/sudoers.d/"
       or (TargetFilePath startswith "/mnt/" and TargetFileName has_any ("runner","sudoers"))
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","bun","sh","bash","tee")
    | extend Source = "FileWrite", ActingProcessCommandLine = ActingProcessCommandLine)
| project TimeGenerated, Source, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Passwordless Sudo Rule Drop via /etc/sudoers.d (Miasma)
id: c4f2a51d-86b3-4c19-9e7a-2d8b6f3c4a91
description: Detects the Miasma payload writing 'NOPASSWD:ALL' rules into /etc/sudoers.d (often via a bind-mount of /mnt), granting passwordless root to the runner/maintainer account.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1548.003
  - attack.t1098
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains: 'NOPASSWD:ALL'
  selection_target:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/etc/sudoers.d'
      - '/mnt/'
      - 'sudoers'
  filter_pkg_install:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/apt'
      - '/dpkg'
      - '/yum'
      - '/dnf'
      - '/rpm'
  condition: selection_cmd and selection_target and not filter_pkg_install
falsepositives:
  - Configuration management (Ansible, Chef, Puppet) deploying sudoers fragments
  - Cloud-init / packer image bake steps writing CI runner sudo rules
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:*NOPASSWD\:ALL* (@process.command_line:*\/etc\/sudoers.d* OR @process.command_line:*\/mnt\/* OR @process.command_line:*sudoers*) -@process.executable.path:(/usr/bin/apt OR /usr/bin/dpkg OR /usr/bin/yum OR /usr/bin/dnf) -@process.command_line:*ansible*
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten)
| (regex("NOPASSWD:ALL", field=CommandLine) AND regex("(/etc/sudoers\\.d|/mnt/|sudoers)", field=CommandLine))
   OR (TargetFileName=/\/etc\/sudoers\.d\// OR TargetFileName=/\/mnt\/(runner|sudoers)/)
| ContextImageFileName=/\/(node|bun|sh|bash|tee|cp|dd)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*NOPASSWD:ALL*" AND (Processes.process="*/etc/sudoers.d*" OR Processes.process="*/mnt/*" OR Processes.process="*runner ALL=(ALL)*")) OR (Processes.process_name="mount" AND Processes.process="*bind*" AND Processes.process="*/etc/sudoers.d*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*NOPASSWD:ALL*" AND (Processes.process="*/etc/sudoers.d*" OR Processes.process="*/mnt/*" OR Processes.process="*runner ALL=(ALL)*")) OR (Processes.process_name="mount" AND Processes.process="*bind*" AND Processes.process="*/etc/sudoers.d*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] Security vendor domain blackhole written to /etc/hosts from non-admin process Exploitation High
Detects the Miasma payload's defense-evasion step where it pipes 'echo 127.0.0.1 <vendor>' through sudo to append to /etc/hosts, blackholing telemetry/update domains for installed security products. Anchored on /etc/hosts writes initiated by node/bun/shell processes. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim code block: 'sudo sh -c "echo \'127.0.0.1 <vendor>\' >> /etc/hosts"' under the Neutralize Security product monitoring comment. The combination of /etc/hosts + 127.0.0.1 + append from a node/bun/sh parent on a CI runner is highly article-specific.
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1565.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "/etc/hosts"
       and ProcessCommandLine has "127.0.0.1"
       and ProcessCommandLine has_any (">>"," tee ","echo ")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun","sh","bash","dash","zsh","sudo")
       or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node","bun","npm")
    | extend Source = "ProcessCreate"),
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FolderPath == "/etc/" and FileName == "hosts"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun","sh","bash","dash","tee","sudo")
    | extend Source = "FileWrite", ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, Source, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
union
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "/etc/hosts"
       and ActingProcessCommandLine has "127.0.0.1"
       and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (">>"," tee ","echo ")
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","bun","sh","bash","sudo")
    | extend Source = "ProcessCreate"),
  (ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where TargetFilePath == "/etc/hosts"
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","bun","sh","bash","tee")
    | extend Source = "FileWrite", ActingProcessCommandLine = ActingProcessCommandLine)
| project TimeGenerated, Source, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: /etc/hosts Blackhole Write from Node or Bun Process (Miasma Defense Evasion)
id: 7e3a1b94-c52f-4d68-b1ae-9f4d8c2e7b15
description: Detects the Miasma payload writing 127.0.0.1 entries to /etc/hosts (typically to blackhole security vendor update/telemetry domains) via a node/bun/shell pipeline using echo + sudo + redirect.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1562.001
  - attack.t1565.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_target:
    CommandLine|contains: '/etc/hosts'
  selection_loopback:
    CommandLine|contains: '127.0.0.1'
  selection_write:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '>>'
      - ' tee '
      - 'echo '
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/node'
      - '/bun'
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/sudo'
      - '/npm'
  condition: selection_target and selection_loopback and selection_write and selection_parent
falsepositives:
  - Container build steps adding loopback overrides in Dockerfile RUN
  - Internal IT scripts overriding DNS for staging environments
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:*\/etc\/hosts* @process.command_line:*127.0.0.1* (@process.command_line:*\>\>* OR @process.command_line:*tee* OR @process.command_line:*echo*) (@process.parent.name:(node OR bun OR sh OR bash OR sudo OR npm) OR @ParentImage:(*\node OR *\bun OR *\sh OR *\bash))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| regex("/etc/hosts", field=CommandLine)
| regex("127\\.0\\.0\\.1", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(>>|\\stee\\s|echo\\s)", field=CommandLine)
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(node|bun|sh|bash|dash|sudo|npm)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/etc/hosts*" AND Processes.process="*127.0.0.1*" AND (Processes.process="*>>*" OR Processes.process="*tee*" OR Processes.process_name="echo") AND (Processes.parent_process_name="node" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bun" OR Processes.parent_process_name="sh" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bash") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/etc/hosts*" AND Processes.process="*127.0.0.1*" AND (Processes.process="*>>*" OR Processes.process="*tee*" OR Processes.process_name="echo") AND (Processes.parent_process_name="node" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bun" OR Processes.parent_process_name="sh" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bash") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] Public GitHub repo creation matching Miasma 'adjective-creature-N' exfil pattern Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the Miasma exfiltration channel: creation of a public GitHub repository under a victim's account named with the adjective-creature-N convention and/or containing the 'Miasma: The Spreading Blight' description, followed by commits to results/<timestamp>-<counter>.json paths. Pivots on CloudAppEvents / GitHub audit logs. Rationale: Anchored on Phase 10 of the article: 'Creates a public repo in the victim’s GitHub account ("Miasma: The Spreading Blight") and commits stolen credential JSON to results/<timestamp>-<counter>.json' and the adjective-creature-<0-99999> naming convention called out in the kill-chain reconstruction. Both the regex name pattern and the 'Miasma' string have no legitimate use in this org's GitHub footprint.
ATT&CKT1567.001 T1102.002
Data sourcesWeb
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where Application has "GitHub"
| where ActionType has_any ("Create repository","RepositoryCreate","repo.create")
| extend RepoName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).repo)
| extend Visibility = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).visibility)
| extend Description = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).description)
| where Visibility =~ "public"
| where RepoName matches regex @"^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-\d{1,5}$"
   or Description has_any ("Miasma","Spreading Blight","The Spreading Blight")
   or RawEventData has "results/" and RawEventData has ".json"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, RepoName, Visibility, Description, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
// Pre-req: GitHub Enterprise audit log connector ingesting into a custom GitHubAudit_CL table, or using OfficeActivity for GitHub via Cloud App Security
let GitHubLogs = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where OfficeWorkload has_any ("GitHub","github")
           or RecordType has "GitHub";
GitHubLogs
| where Operation has_any ("repo.create","RepositoryCreate","Create repository")
| extend RepoName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).repo)
| extend Visibility = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).visibility)
| extend Description = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).description)
| where Visibility =~ "public"
| where RepoName matches regex @"^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-\d{1,5}$"
   or Description has_any ("Miasma","Spreading Blight")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, RepoName, Visibility, Description, Operation
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:github @action:(repo.create OR RepositoryCreate) @repo.visibility:public (@repo.name:/^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-\d{1,5}$/ OR @repo.description:(*Miasma* OR *"Spreading Blight"*))
CLOUD
`github_audit_log` action="repo.create" visibility="public" (repo="*-*-*" OR description="*Miasma*" OR description="*Spreading Blight*") | rex field=repo "^(?<adj>[a-z]+)-(?<creature>[a-z]+)-(?<idx>\d{1,5})$" | where isnotnull(idx) AND idx>=0 AND idx<=99999 | stats min(_time) as firstSeen, count by user, repo, description, visibility | sort - firstSeen
[LLM] Worm-injected .github/setup.js commit with 'chore: update dependencies [skip ci]' message Actions on Objectives High
Detects the Miasma worm's lateral-movement technique: commits adding a .github/setup.js file via the GitHub Git Data API, authored as 'github-actions@github.com' with the verbatim message 'chore: update dependencies [skip ci]'. These commits appear across non-protected branches in victim-owned repos and skip CI by design. Rationale: Anchored on Phase 11 of the kill-chain reconstruction: 'Hunt for commits adding .github/setup.js authored as github-actions@github.com with message chore: update dependencies [skip ci]'. The exact file path, author email, and commit message are verbatim worm signatures with no legitimate corollary — Dependabot uses a different author identity and never adds setup.js.
ATT&CKT1080 T1195.002 T1098.004
Data sourcesChange
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where Application has "GitHub"
| where ActionType has_any ("git.push","push","PushCommit","Push")
| extend Files = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).added)
| extend Message = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).message)
| extend AuthorEmail = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).author_email)
| where Files has ".github/setup.js"
   or (Message =~ "chore: update dependencies [skip ci]" and AuthorEmail =~ "github-actions@github.com")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, ObjectName, Files, Message, AuthorEmail, IPAddress, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
let GitHubLogs = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where OfficeWorkload has "GitHub" or RecordType has "GitHub";
GitHubLogs
| where Operation has_any ("git.push","push","PushCommit")
| extend Files = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).added)
| extend Message = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).message)
| extend AuthorEmail = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).author_email)
| where Files has ".github/setup.js"
   or (Message =~ "chore: update dependencies [skip ci]" and AuthorEmail =~ "github-actions@github.com")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ObjectId, Files, Message, AuthorEmail, ClientIP
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Miasma Worm .github/setup.js Injection Commit
id: 9d1f5c83-2a47-4b96-8e1c-3f7a8b9d6e21
description: Detects commits that add .github/setup.js with the Miasma worm's signature author 'github-actions@github.com' and message 'chore: update dependencies [skip ci]'. This is the worm's mechanism to spread laterally across victim-owned GitHub repos via the Git Data API.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/
author: Detection Engineering

detection:

  selection_author_msg:
    commit_author_email: 'github-actions@github.com'
    commit_message: 'chore: update dependencies [skip ci]'

  - Internal automation legitimately authoring as github-actions@github.com to update workflows
level: high
source:github @action:(git.push OR push OR PushCommit) (@commit.added:*.github\/setup.js* OR (@commit.author.email:github-actions@github.com AND @commit.message:"chore: update dependencies [skip ci]"))
CLOUD
`github_audit_log` (action="git.push" OR action="push") (commit_message="chore: update dependencies [skip ci]" OR added_files="*.github/setup.js*") | rex max_match=1 field=added_files "(?<setupjs>\.github/setup\.js)" | where isnotnull(setupjs) OR (commit_author_email="github-actions@github.com" AND commit_message="chore: update dependencies [skip ci]") | stats min(_time) as firstSeen, dc(repo) as repoCount, values(repo) as repos by user, commit_author_email | sort - firstSeen
[LLM] Destructive 'rm -rf ~' or Miasma honeytoken tripwire from node/bun process tree Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the Miasma destructive fail-safe: 'rm -rf ~/' / 'rm -rf ~/Documents' invoked by a node or bun process tree (often after the planted honeytoken 'IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner' is touched). Also directly matches the honeytoken string in any process command line or file content. Rationale: Anchored on Phase 12 of the kill-chain reconstruction: the verbatim honeytoken string 'IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner' and the destructive commands 'rm -rf ~/' and 'rm -rf ~/Documents'. The honeytoken string is unique to this campaign with zero legitimate use; the rm-rf combined with a node/bun parent is the article's specific destructive-tripwire shape, distinguishing it from generic CI workspace cleanup.
ATT&CKT1485 T1491.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName in~ ("rm","rm.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "-rf"
          and (ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\s~/?(\s|$)"
               or ProcessCommandLine has " $HOME"
               or ProcessCommandLine has "~/Documents"
               or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\s/home/[^/\s]+/?(\s|$)"))
      or ProcessCommandLine has "IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun","sh","bash","dash","zsh","npm")
     or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node","bun","npm","yarn","pnpm")
     or ProcessCommandLine has "IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, 
    InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
    InitiatingProcessParentCreationTime
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (ActingProcessName endswith "rm" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "-rf"
          and (ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\s~/?(\s|$)"
               or ActingProcessCommandLine has " $HOME"
               or ActingProcessCommandLine has "~/Documents"))
      or ActingProcessCommandLine has "IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","bun","sh","bash","npm")
     or ActingProcessCommandLine has "IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"

        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7") or SHA1 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7") or MD5 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7") or SHA1 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7") or MD5 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Article-specific behavioural hunt — Preinstall to persistence: Inside the Red Hat npm Miasma credential-stealing cam Exploitation High
Auto-generated hunt targeting the specific binaries, paths, registry locations and command-line fragments named in this article. Hunting tier — needs analyst review and environment tuning before promotion to alerting.
ATT&CKT1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
// Article-specific bespoke detection — Preinstall to persistence: Inside the Red Hat npm Miasma credential-stealing cam
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("index.js", "node.js", "bun.exe", "npm.cmd") or FolderPath has_any ("\AppData\Local\Temp"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("\AppData\Local\Temp", "/etc/hosts", "/etc/sudoers.d", "/tmp/b-", "/tmp/p.") or FileName in~ ("index.js", "node.js", "bun.exe", "npm.cmd"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Article-specific bespoke detection — Preinstall to persistence: Inside the Red Hat npm Miasma credential-stealing cam ```
| tstats `summariesonly` count earliest(_time) AS firstTime latest(_time) AS lastTime

[LLM] Java process beaconing to WeedHack C2 infrastructure Command & Control High
Detects java.exe/javaw.exe initiating outbound network sessions to the WeedHack receiver/remote-control domains or the staging IP 45.141.119.34. Because the C2 hosts are dedicated to the MaaS dashboard, any hit from a Java parent is high-fidelity infostealer beacon or premium-tier RAT traffic. Rationale: Both the IP 45.141.119.34 and the receiver.*/whreceive.*/telemetrydata.to host set are named in the article and corroborated by McAfee Labs and CyberInsider write-ups. Scoping by java.exe/javaw.exe parent yields near-zero baseline FP because legitimate Java apps don't dial .cy/.ru receivers. Cross-checked against: • https://www.mcafee.com/blogs/other-blogs/mcafee-labs/weedhack-minecraft-malware-as-a-service-campaign-research/ • https://cyberinsider.com/weedhack-minecraft-malware-campaign-infects-over-116000-pcs/ • https://0xresetti.github.io/weedhack.html

| where RemoteIP == "45.141.119.34"
    or RemoteUrl has_any ("receiver.cy","whreceive.ru","whreceiver.ru","remotev2.whreceive.ru","telemetrydata.to")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr == "45.141.119.34"
    or DstHostname has_any ("receiver.cy","whreceive.ru","whreceiver.ru","remotev2.whreceive.ru","telemetrydata.to")
| where SrcUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol, Url
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] DNS / web resolution of WeedHack distribution and C2 domains Delivery High
Org-wide signal on any DNS query or web request to the WeedHack distribution sites (weedhack.cy, weedhack.to, marsalek.cy, huehnchenfarm.ru) or receiver C2 hosts. Catches the lure-site visit phase before the JAR is ever executed and works even on hosts without EDR. Rationale: Both the distribution domains (weedhack.cy, weedhack.to, marsalek.cy, huehnchenfarm.ru) and the receiver/C2 set are explicitly listed in the article's pre-extracted IOCs and re-confirmed in the McAfee Labs blog and 0xresetti's WeedHack technical analysis. Domain-IOC alerting carries near-zero FP because the names are unique and unrelated to legitimate Minecraft infrastructure. Cross-checked against: • https://www.mcafee.com/blogs/other-blogs/mcafee-labs/weedhack-minecraft-malware-as-a-service-campaign-research/ • https://0xresetti.github.io/weedhack.html • https://cyberinsider.com/weedhack-minecraft-malware-campaign-infects-over-116000-pcs/
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1583.008 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
let WeedHackIOCs = dynamic(["weedhack.cy","weedhack.to","marsalek.cy","huehnchenfarm.ru","receiver.cy","whreceive.ru","whreceiver.ru","remotev2.whreceive.ru","telemetrydata.to"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (WeedHackIOCs) or RemoteIP == "45.141.119.34"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Source = "DeviceNetworkEvents"),
  (DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse" and RemoteUrl has_any (WeedHackIOCs)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort = int(null), Source = "DnsQueryResponse")
| order by Timestamp desc
let WeedHackIOCs = dynamic(["weedhack.cy","weedhack.to","marsalek.cy","huehnchenfarm.ru","receiver.cy","whreceive.ru","whreceiver.ru","remotev2.whreceive.ru","telemetrydata.to"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name has_any (WeedHackIOCs)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, IPAddresses, Source = "DnsEvents"),
  (ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (WeedHackIOCs)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, ClientIP = SrcIpAddr, Name = DnsQuery, QueryType = DnsQueryTypeName, IPAddresses = DnsResponseName, Source = "ImDnsActivity"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where RequestURL has_any (WeedHackIOCs) or DestinationHostName has_any (WeedHackIOCs) or DestinationIP == "45.141.119.34"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = SourceHostName, ClientIP = SourceIP, Name = coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), QueryType = ApplicationProtocol, IPAddresses = DestinationIP, Source = "CommonSecurityLog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Java executing Minecraft-client-named JAR from Downloads or Temp Installation Medium
Hunts java.exe/javaw.exe spawned with a JAR file path whose name matches the lure-client list called out by McAfee (Meteor, Wurst, Aristois, LiquidBounce, Impact, Skytils, Radium, Future, Inertia, Cornos, WWE, 3arthh4ck, Salhack, Phobos, Gamesense) and that lives under user Downloads, Temp, or .minecraft\mods. Catches the WeedHack detonation moment. Rationale: The 14-name lure list is verbatim from the article's SEO-poisoning paragraph plus Skytils called out in the screenshot, and the download paths are from the kill-chain Phase 2 detection hint. Pairing client-name + downloads-path-prefix is the article-specific combination — a power user might run java with a JAR, but the specific named lures from this campaign in Downloads/Temp is high-signal. Cross-checked against: • https://www.mcafee.com/blogs/other-blogs/mcafee-labs/weedhack-minecraft-malware-as-a-service-campaign-research/ • https://0xresetti.github.io/weedhack.html

title: WeedHack Minecraft Lure JAR Executed by Java
id: 2b7c5f49-90a1-4d3e-b6f7-1e2d09f4ac38
description: Detects java.exe/javaw.exe launching a JAR whose name matches a known Minecraft client targeted by WeedHack (Meteor/Wurst/Aristois/LiquidBounce/etc.) from user Downloads, Temp, or .minecraft\mods.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/over-116-000-minecraft-systems-infected-in-weedhack-malware-campaign/
  - https://www.mcafee.com/blogs/other-blogs/mcafee-labs/weedhack-minecraft-malware-as-a-service-campaign-research/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1059.006
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\java.exe'
      - '\javaw.exe'
  selection_jar:
    CommandLine|contains: '.jar'
  selection_path:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '\Downloads\'
      - '\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
      - '\.minecraft\mods\'
  selection_lure:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Meteor'
      - 'Wurst'
      - 'Aristois'
      - 'LiquidBounce'
      - 'Impact'
      - 'Skytils'
      - 'Radium'
      - 'Future'
      - 'Inertia'
      - 'Cornos'
      - 'WWE'
      - '3arthh4ck'
      - 'Salhack'
      - 'Phobos'
      - 'Gamesense'
  condition: all of selection_*
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\java.exe OR *\javaw.exe OR *\Java.exe OR *\JAVA.EXE OR *\JavaW.exe OR *\JAVAW.EXE) @CommandLine:(*Downloads* OR *\\Temp\\* OR *AppData\\Local\\Temp* OR *.minecraft\\mods*) @CommandLine:(*Meteor* OR *Wurst* OR *Aristois* OR *LiquidBounce* OR *Impact* OR *Skytils* OR *Radium* OR *Future* OR *Inertia* OR *Cornos* OR *3arthh4ck* OR *Salhack* OR *Phobos* OR *Gamesense*) @CommandLine:*.jar*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\java(w)?\.exe$/i
| regex("\\.jar", field=CommandLine)
| regex("\\\\(Downloads|Temp|AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp|\\.minecraft\\\\mods)\\\\", field=CommandLine)
| CommandLine=/(Meteor|Wurst|Aristois|LiquidBounce|Impact|Skytils|Radium|Future|Inertia|Cornos|3arthh4ck|Salhack|Phobos|Gamesense)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parents from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("java.exe","javaw.exe") AND Processes.process IN ("*\\Downloads\\*.jar*","*\\Temp\\*.jar*","*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*.jar*","*\\.minecraft\\mods\\*.jar*") AND Processes.process IN ("*Meteor*","*Wurst*","*Aristois*","*LiquidBounce*","*Impact*","*Skytils*","*Radium*","*Future*","*Inertia*","*Cornos*","*WWE*","*3arthh4ck*","*Salhack*","*Phobos*","*Gamesense*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parents from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("java.exe","javaw.exe") AND Processes.process IN ("*\\Downloads\\*.jar*","*\\Temp\\*.jar*","*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*.jar*","*\\.minecraft\\mods\\*.jar*") AND Processes.process IN ("*Meteor*","*Wurst*","*Aristois*","*LiquidBounce*","*Impact*","*Skytils*","*Radium*","*Future*","*Inertia*","*Cornos*","*WWE*","*3arthh4ck*","*Salhack*","*Phobos*","*Gamesense*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] Java process reading browser, Discord, Steam or Telegram credential stores Actions on Objectives High
Hunts for java.exe/javaw.exe touching the specific credential-storage files WeedHack targets: Chromium Login Data / Cookies / Local State across 36 browsers, Discord leveldb, Steam ssfn / config.vdf, Telegram tdata, and wallet-extension Local Extension Settings. No legitimate Java process needs to read these paths. Rationale: The credential-store path set comes directly from kill-chain Phase 4: '36 browsers, 56 cryptocurrency add-ons, 12 desktop cryptocurrency wallet apps, Discord, Steam, and Telegram credentials'. McAfee's report and 0xresetti's reverse-engineering confirm the stealer enumerates Chromium User Data\*\Login Data, Discord leveldb, Steam ssfn, and Telegram tdata. Threshold of 2+ distinct paths avoids single-file-read FPs from legit Java apps. Cross-checked against: • https://www.mcafee.com/blogs/other-blogs/mcafee-labs/weedhack-minecraft-malware-as-a-service-campaign-research/ • https://0xresetti.github.io/weedhack.html
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1539 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let CredPaths = dynamic([@"\Login Data", @"\Cookies", @"\Local State", @"\discord\Local Storage\leveldb", @"\discordcanary\Local Storage\leveldb", @"\discordptb\Local Storage\leveldb", @"\Steam\config\config.vdf", @"\Steam\ssfn", @"\Steam\config\loginusers.vdf", @"\Telegram Desktop\tdata", @"\Local Extension Settings\"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java.exe","javaw.exe")
| where FolderPath has_any (CredPaths)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize HitCount = count(), DistinctPaths = dcount(FolderPath), SamplePaths = make_set(FolderPath, 10), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| where DistinctPaths >= 2
| order by LastSeen desc
let CredPaths = dynamic([@"\Login Data", @"\Cookies", @"\Local State", @"\discord\Local Storage\leveldb", @"\Steam\config\config.vdf", @"\Steam\ssfn", @"\Telegram Desktop\tdata", @"\Local Extension Settings\"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith @"\java.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith @"\javaw.exe"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (CredPaths)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| summarize HitCount = count(), DistinctPaths = dcount(TargetFilePath), SamplePaths = make_set(TargetFilePath, 10), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
          by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessCommandLine
| where DistinctPaths >= 2
| order by LastSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\java.exe OR *\javaw.exe OR *\Java.exe OR *\JAVA.EXE OR *\JavaW.exe OR *\JAVAW.EXE) @TargetFilename:(*\\Login\ Data* OR *\\Cookies* OR *\\Local\ State* OR *\\discord\\Local\ Storage\\leveldb* OR *\\Steam\\ssfn* OR *\\Steam\\config\\config.vdf OR *\\Telegram\ Desktop\\tdata* OR *\\Local\ Extension\ Settings*)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/\\java(w)?\.exe$/i
| TargetFileName=/\\(Login Data|Cookies|Local State|discord\\Local Storage\\leveldb|Steam\\ssfn|Steam\\config\\config\.vdf|Telegram Desktop\\tdata|Local Extension Settings)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, UserName], function={ DistinctPaths := count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true) | HitCount := count() })
| DistinctPaths > 1
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("java.exe","javaw.exe") AND Filesystem.file_path IN ("*\\User Data\\*\\Login Data*","*\\User Data\\*\\Cookies*","*\\User Data\\*\\Network\\Cookies*","*\\User Data\\Local State*","*\\discord\\Local Storage\\leveldb\\*","*\\discordcanary\\Local Storage\\leveldb\\*","*\\discordptb\\Local Storage\\leveldb\\*","*\\Steam\\config\\config.vdf","*\\Steam\\ssfn*","*\\Steam\\config\\loginusers.vdf","*\\Telegram Desktop\\tdata\\*","*\\Local Extension Settings\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_guid | where count > 3 | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("java.exe","javaw.exe") AND Filesystem.file_path IN ("*\\User Data\\*\\Login Data*","*\\User Data\\*\\Cookies*","*\\User Data\\*\\Network\\Cookies*","*\\User Data\\Local State*","*\\discord\\Local Storage\\leveldb\\*","*\\discordcanary\\Local Storage\\leveldb\\*","*\\discordptb\\Local Storage\\leveldb\\*","*\\Steam\\config\\config.vdf","*\\Steam\\ssfn*","*\\Steam\\config\\loginusers.vdf","*\\Telegram Desktop\\tdata\\*","*\\Local Extension Settings\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_guid | where count > 3 | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
[LLM] JAR file written to disk with WeedHack distribution URL provenance Delivery High
Catches the delivery moment — a .jar dropped by a browser (chrome.exe/msedge.exe/firefox.exe/brave.exe) where FileOriginUrl or FileOriginReferrerUrl points to a WeedHack distribution domain. Targets the SEO-poisoning and YouTube-comment-link arrival path before java is even invoked. Rationale: Combines file extension (.jar), browser parent, and FileOriginUrl-derived provenance — three article-specific anchors. The WeedHack distribution domains are unique to this campaign per McAfee Labs and 0xresetti's analysis, so any browser-downloaded JAR with this provenance is effectively a confirmed delivery. Cross-checked against: • https://www.mcafee.com/blogs/other-blogs/mcafee-labs/weedhack-minecraft-malware-as-a-service-campaign-research/ • https://0xresetti.github.io/weedhack.html • https://cyberinsider.com/weedhack-minecraft-malware-campaign-infects-over-116000-pcs/
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.002 T1608.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let WeedHackDistro = dynamic(["weedhack.cy","weedhack.to","marsalek.cy","huehnchenfarm.ru","receiver.cy"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where FileName endswith ".jar"
| where (FileOriginUrl has_any (WeedHackDistro) or FileOriginReferrerUrl has_any (WeedHackDistro))
   or  (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","vivaldi.exe") and (FileOriginUrl has_any (WeedHackDistro) or FileOriginReferrerUrl has_any (WeedHackDistro)))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, FileSize, FileOriginUrl, FileOriginReferrerUrl, FileOriginIP
| order by Timestamp desc
let WeedHackDistro = dynamic(["weedhack.cy","weedhack.to","marsalek.cy","huehnchenfarm.ru","receiver.cy"]);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has_any (WeedHackDistro)
| where FileName endswith ".jar" or Url endswith ".jar"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, Url, FileName, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpResponseBodyBytes, DstHostname
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: JAR Download from WeedHack Distribution Site
id: 4a912bd0-6e58-4f37-bd91-7283c4d05cd2
description: Detects a browser writing a .jar file to disk where the file-origin URL points at a known WeedHack distribution domain.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/over-116-000-minecraft-systems-infected-in-weedhack-malware-campaign/
  - https://www.mcafee.com/blogs/other-blogs/mcafee-labs/weedhack-minecraft-malware-as-a-service-campaign-research/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1566.002
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1608.006
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\brave.exe'
      - '\opera.exe'
      - '\vivaldi.exe'
  selection_ext:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.jar'
  selection_origin:
    Contents|contains:
      - 'weedhack.cy'
      - 'weedhack.to'
      - 'marsalek.cy'
      - 'huehnchenfarm.ru'
      - 'receiver.cy'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_ext and selection_origin
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:15 @TargetFilename:*.jar @Contents:(*weedhack.cy* OR *weedhack.to* OR *marsalek.cy* OR *huehnchenfarm.ru* OR *receiver.cy*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\.jar$/i ContextImageFileName=/\\(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|opera|vivaldi)\.exe$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/^(weedhack\.cy|weedhack\.to|marsalek\.cy|huehnchenfarm\.ru|receiver\.cy)$/i}, field=aid, include=[DomainName])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as files values(Filesystem.file_hash) as hashes from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action=created AND Filesystem.file_name="*.jar" AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","vivaldi.exe") AND Filesystem.file_origin_url IN ("*weedhack.cy*","*weedhack.to*","*marsalek.cy*","*huehnchenfarm.ru*","*receiver.cy*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_origin_url | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as files values(Filesystem.file_hash) as hashes from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action=created AND Filesystem.file_name="*.jar" AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","vivaldi.exe") AND Filesystem.file_origin_url IN ("*weedhack.cy*","*weedhack.to*","*marsalek.cy*","*huehnchenfarm.ru*","*receiver.cy*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_origin_url | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1219
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'
            - '\NinjaOne.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - IT-approved RMM in use across the estate. Maintain a known-IT-
      tool exclusion list per environment.
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("receiver.cy", "weedhack.cy")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["receiver.cy", "weedhack.cy"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Downloader or shell child of npm/pip install (postinstall RAT loader) · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Package manager runtime connecting to durabletask/axios supply-chain C2 IOCs · Network connections to article IPs / domains

Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Lateral movement via aws ssm send-command or kubectl exec spawned by python/node · [LLM] Cloud credential file access by node/python runtime · [LLM] Locale-conditional rm -rf wiper command from python/node runtime
[LLM] Package manager runtime connecting to durabletask/axios supply-chain C2 IOCs Command & Control High
Network connections from node/python/npm/pip processes to the C2 IPs and domains attributed to the March 2026 axios npm hijack and May 2026 durabletask Python backdoor. Pivots on the article's exact infrastructure observables so it survives binary renaming and code refactors. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact C2 IPs (142.11.206.73, 160.119.64.3) and domains (sfrclak.com, check.git-service.com, t.m-kosche.com, packages.npm.org typosquat of packages.npmjs.org). [LLM] Lateral movement via aws ssm send-command or kubectl exec spawned by python/node Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the durabletask post-compromise tradecraft — backdoored Python (or its node equivalent) shelling out to aws/kubectl to spread laterally using the victim's own credentials via SSM SendCommand/StartSession or kubectl exec. The parent-runtime pivot is what makes this article-specific rather than a generic admin-tool detection. Rationale: The article specifies the durabletask backdoor spread 'to other instances over SSM and to other pods via kubectl exec' using the victim's own credentials. Filtering AWS/kubectl execution to a python/node parent makes this an actual supply-chain signal rather than admin-tool noise, and the CloudTrail variant catches the same activity by user-agent footprint when EDR isn't on the host.
ATT&CKT1021.007 T1609 T1078.004

| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","node.exe","python","python3","node")
| where FileName in~ ("aws.exe","aws","kubectl.exe","kubectl")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("ssm send-command","ssm start-session","kubectl exec","exec -it","exec --stdin")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("python","python3","node","python.exe","python3.exe","node.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("aws","aws.exe","kubectl","kubectl.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ssm send-command","ssm start-session","kubectl exec","exec -it","exec --stdin")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Downloader or shell child of npm/pip install (postinstall RAT loader) Installation Medium
Detects the axios-style postinstall pattern where a malicious package's install hook reaches out for a second-stage payload via curl/wget/powershell/bitsadmin. The parent-equals-package-manager pivot turns generic downloader behavior into a supply-chain-specific signal. Rationale: The axios hijack 'added one new dependency whose only job was a postinstall script that pulled down a cross-platform RAT and deleted itself' — the loader behaviour is a download from a non-language-runtime binary spawned by the package manager. Parent==package-manager + child==downloader + URL/download-cmdline is the article's exact shape.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.001 T1105

| where FileName in~ ("curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","bash","sh","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","Invoke-WebRequest","DownloadString","-OutFile","/dev/tcp/","base64 -d")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("npm","pip","pip3","node","python","python3","yarn","pnpm")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("curl","wget","powershell","pwsh","bitsadmin","certutil","bash","sh")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","Invoke-WebRequest","DownloadString","-OutFile","/dev/tcp/","base64 -d")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Cloud credential file access by node/python runtime Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the durabletask second-stage credential harvest where a backdoored Python (or node) runtime reads .aws/credentials, .azure, .kube/config, gcloud config, .vault-token, and .npmrc. Targets the file paths the article enumerates — AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, Vault. Rationale: The article states the durabletask second stage 'harvested credentials from AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, and Vault'. The standard paths for those credential stores (~/.aws/credentials, ~/.kube/config, ~/.azure, ~/.config/gcloud, ~/.vault-token, ~/.npmrc) being touched by node/python is the concrete behaviour. The runtime filter keeps this from firing on AWS CLI / kubectl / az themselves.
